scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

Imported amorua geometry covers 1492 to 1500 over the Colombian-Venezuelan Orinoco region. The card identifies a continuing people and uses explicitly later evidence. It does not validate the historical polygon or manufacture a fifteenth-century state.

The Etnollano Banco del Saber links both community publications publicly. The memory report was read as extracted PDF text; the eight-page Guáripa scan was rendered and relevant pages 2 to 5 visually read. Local copies are research cache files, not redistributed publication assets.

The Guáripa booklet is catalogued as 2014 by CENDAR. Its statement that the community was founded forty years earlier is not converted to an exact year. Its 2005 organizing date is explicit. Rosa Juana is credited as described without inventing a full name or office.

Craft materials, dye examples and coiling are drawn from the visually inspected booklet. The conservation description is the artisans’ account of their practice, not an independent ecological impact assessment.

The food study’s evidence concerns La Esmeralda in Caño Mochuelo, with fieldwork in 2013 and 2014. The sebucán is supported by the textual discussion and caption; the corresponding photograph was not independently inspected. No archaeological excavation is claimed.

Food transport arrangements and changing river conditions are dated fieldwork observations, not current 2026 measurements. Local availability categories in the report are not treated as global species extinction.

Gobierno Mayor’s broad housing and leadership descriptions are explicitly attributed. Its conflation of other peoples as alternative Amorúa names and language simplifications are not adopted, nor is its hierarchy of supposedly more developed cultures.

The 2014 academic article was read through its public Dialnet full-text mirror. Its Amorúa fieldwork dates to 2013; the separate Wayúu evidence and Bahía Portete massacre are not assigned to the Amorúa.

The education report records a multi-people program. Aggregate numbers and curriculum implementation are not presented as exclusively Amorúa outcomes. The card does not assume every planned educational result was completed.

The SENA report groups named Amorúa and Sikuani artisans without matching each person to a people; no such match is invented. The precise July day is omitted because its weekday/date combination is inconsistent.

The Unidad para las Víctimas report concerns the shared Kanalitojo community. Its statement of completed measures is attributed, not a claim that all conflict harms disappeared. The community’s continued organization does not require a fabricated fall year or conqueror.
Independent historical review, identity/border verification and depth certification remain pending.
